revision_note: v2 corrects the wording of the verdict and adds the review the focal point asked for. The verdict is BLOCKED_TARGET_NOT_VISIBLE: what was measured is that the current EventKit enumeration does not contain the target, and nothing here establishes that the list was deleted or that it left the account. Account change, sync lag, identity change, a list sitting in Recently Deleted and a source-scope change are all left open. It also answers why two lists came back when the application promised one: the promise was wrong, /reminders/lists is account-wide, and the harness had encoded the same wrong promise as a hard precondition, so the window was blocked by two independent causes. The suggestion to count items in other lists is removed - it widened the data scope for no diagnostic gain. No new real read was performed for this revision.
executed_by: WorkBuddy engineering agent (sole engineering executor for this task)
authorization: R1 real diagnostic authorized by the focal point at 2026-11-10, scope A1-A9, single 45-minute session, cumulative gate-open budget <= 600s. That window is closed and is not extended by this revision.
verdict_assertion: The bound list 9D9A****03F3 is not present in the reminder-calendar enumeration that the bridge returned on 2026-11-10T14:45:13Z: HTTP 200, two entries, neither of them the target. That is the whole of the finding. This receipt does not assert that the list was deleted, that it left the account, or that the account changed - only that it is not visible to EventKit on MAC-1 right now. A second, independent cause also blocked the same window: the harness required exactly one visible list, which this account can never satisfy (see why_two_lists).

decisive_measurement.interpretation: HTTP 200 proves the request was authorized and the Reminders dataclass is readable, so the enumeration is meaningful rather than an empty or denied answer. Two calendars came back and neither carries the bound identifier. Whether that is because the list no longer exists, was never synced to this Mac, lives under a different account now, or is merely not enumerated is not decided by this measurement.

why_two_lists.question: The application promised that GET /reminders/lists returns only the single bound list. It returned two. Which is wrong, the promise or the observation?
why_two_lists.answer: The promise. The endpoint is account-wide by construction, and the observation is the correct behaviour of the deployed binary.

source_evidence.claim: .listReminders calls store.fetchListsMetadata() and encodes the result directly. There is no allowlistValidator call on this branch.
The allowlist runs only on the item branch: .getReminders(listID:) does try allowlistValidator.validate(listID:) before touching content.
The enumeration is store.calendars(for: .reminder) mapped one-to-one. No filtering, no dedupe, no per-source scoping.
Each entry carries listID, title, sourceID, sourceType, sourceName, color, isImmutable. reminderCount and all content fields are deliberately absent (FIX-R4A-01).

why_two_lists.behavioural_evidence: The allowlist in the running configuration has exactly one entry (static_config: allowed_list_count=1, allowed_list_matches_target=true) while the enumeration returned two calendars. Two entries with a one-entry allowlist is only possible if this endpoint does not filter by allowlist. B2 saw three entries under the same one-entry allowlist, which points the same way.
fields_actually_returned: listID (full, unmasked, for every list in the account)
title (full, unmasked, for every list in the account)
NOT returned: reminder counts, item titles, item notes, dates, completed flags

non_target_metadata.what_the_client_discarded: The other entries' titles and identifiers, in memory, before any write. Discarding happens at the persistence layer only: the server did read them and did return them over the wire, and that is not changed by what the client chose to keep.

non_target_metadata.wording_correction: An earlier draft of this receipt, and of the R1-02 application, implied that only the target's metadata was touched. That is true of the evidence files and false of the transport: GET /reminders/lists is account-wide on the server side. 'Only the target' now means 'only the target is persisted', and nothing stronger.

deployment_evidence_boundary.statement: F7 still holds: the deployed artifact f78e24e5...3074 cannot be tied to a source commit from archived evidence, so 'the source says X' is not by itself a statement about the running binary.
deployment_evidence_boundary.what_closes_it_here: Two behavioural pairs that only agree if the deployed branch matches the source on this point: one allowlist entry with two enumerated lists now, and one allowlist entry with three enumerated lists on 2026-11-07. A build that filtered this endpoint by allowlist would have returned one entry in both cases.
deployment_evidence_boundary.what_stays_open: Agreement on this branch says nothing about branches not exercised: masking, ordering, error mapping and the item path are outside what this observation constrains. The claim is narrow on purpose.

harness_consequence.defect: Client 2.1.0 asserted single_visible_list (len(lists) == 1) as a precondition and exited 20 whenever it failed, in the same branch as a missing target.
harness_consequence.effect: On this account the capture could not have proceeded even if the target had been present - two other lists alone were enough to exit 20.
harness_consequence.consequence_for_this_verdict: The window's exit 20 is over-determined: target absent AND an unsatisfiable precondition. The target's absence is measured independently (target_visible=false) and stands on its own, but the statement 'the window stopped because the target is missing' would be incomplete.
harness_consequence.fix: Client 2.2.0 drops the single-list assertion, records the account-wide count as context, and gates only on the target's presence. The exit code and classification are unchanged, so the old evidence stays readable.
harness_consequence.offline_verification: test_r1_bridge_client.py scenario 11 now covers both halves: target present among two lists proceeds and still persists no other list's title or identifier; target absent among two lists is the only thing that exits 20.

why_two_lists.correction_to_the_application: Section 6 of the application stated that the endpoint is allowlist-bound and returns only the bound list. That was wrong and has been struck through and corrected in place (section 6, item 1) rather than quietly deleted.

bridge.env wraps the value in double quotes. The documented awk produced 66 bytes including the quotes, which failed authentication with 401 instead of 403 on the first preflight. Fixed at the sink and at the source: read_token() now refuses a still-quoted value with a named TokenFileError, and scripts/r1_token_extract.sh normalises quoting, CRLF and whitespace with hard refusals on ambiguity. Offline: scripts/tests/test_r1_token_extract.sh, 24/24.

BLOCKED_TARGET_LIST_ABSENT is withdrawn. It carried a causal claim (the list left the account) that the measurement does not support. The verdict is BLOCKED_TARGET_NOT_VISIBLE, and the snapshot of unexcluded possibilities is written out in full in this receipt.

Section 6 of the application claimed /reminders/lists is allowlist-bound. It is not; only the item endpoint is. Corrected in place with the source lines cited, and the consequence for identity evidence stated: identity is established by locating the target inside the returned set, not by the set having one entry.
